chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) who had intercourse with his wife, and he said: 'He is in the same position as one who broke his fast for a day in the month of Ramadan.'

key_terms.الْمُعْتَكِفِ: The person performing i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque for worship)
key_terms.وَاقَعَ أَهْلَهُ: He had intercourse with his wife/spouse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone in i'tikaf who has intercourse with their wife?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) equates the penalty for sexual intercourse during i'tikaf to breaking a single day of Ramadan fasting, highlighting the severity of disrupting the spiritual state of the mosque. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that while the act invalidates the i'tikaf, the expiation (kaffarah) is proportional to the breach of sanctity rather than the maximum penalty for major sins. The comparison to Ramadan fasting underscores the continuity of ritual purity and devotion required in both practices.
